title: An animal model of EPO-induced abdominal aortic aneurysm in WT and Apoe-/- mice
protocol: Calculate the injection volume for each mouse based on grouping and body weight.
Give the control group normal saline via intraperitoneal injection.
Perform EPO injection in a dark place.
Grab the fur on the mouse’s hackles and secure the head to prevent a bite.
Fix the tail of the mouse with the ring finger or little thumb of the left hand.
Grasp the mouse carefully for injection.
Insert the needle slowly into the mouse abdomen at an angle between 30 and 45 degrees, ensuring the depth is less than 1 cm.
Draw back the syringe slightly to confirm negative pressure indicating correct placement in the abdominal cavity.
Inject the prepared EPO solution or other working solutions (as per treatment) into the abdominal cavity.
Rotate the needle gently before slowly pulling it out to prevent leakage.
Monitor mice daily for diet intake, water drinking, behavior, health status and deaths during injection periods.
Monitor WT mice for large abdominal aortic hematomas.
Monitor Apoe−/− mice for bilateral lower limb paralysis and dissecting aneurysms.
Euthanize mice exhibiting severe symptoms such as massive intra-abdominal hemorrhage or large abdominal aortic hematoma.
Perform autopsy on suddenly deceased mice to determine cause of death.
Anesthetize mice with intraperitoneal injection of sodium pentobarbital (80 mg/kg).
Euthanize mice by cervical dislocation after deep reflex has disappeared.
Fix the mice on the bench.
Cut the abdominal skin with a U-shape incision.
Open the abdominal cavity carefully to avoid liver damage.
Cut the diaphragm along the edge of the ribs.
Bluntly isolate the fatty tissue around the heart and pericardium to expose the heart clearly.
Draw about 1.5 mL of blood from the apical part of the heart using a sterile syringe (1 mL or 2 mL).
Drop a small amount of blood into an EDTA-containing anticoagulation tube.
Flick the wall of the tube to mix the blood well for whole blood testing.
Place the remaining blood in a procoagulant tube at 25°C for 30 min.
Centrifuge the blood at 900 g for 15 min.
Collect the serum and store it at -80°C.
Cut and open the right auricle.
Perform in vivo perfusion using normal saline (approximately 20 mL).
Isolate the heart, liver, spleen, kidney, and aorta.
Prepare isolated liver and kidney into paraffin sections.
Stain sections with H&E to observe morphological changes in liver and kidney tissue after EPO injection.
Measure heart and spleen weights to assess impact of EPO injections.
Evaluate plaque area in aortic root cross-sections by H&E and oil red O staining if Apoe−/− mice are used.
Use stereo microscope when separating periaortic connective tissue.
Soak vascular tissue in cold normal saline to prevent degradation.
Isolate entire aorta from ascending aorta to iliac artery, preferably preserving right and left common carotid arteries and the left subclavian artery.
Measure external diameters of abdominal aorta using vernier caliper.
Take photographs of entire aorta.
Define AAA as localized dilation of abdominal aorta with an external diameter exceeding normal aortic diameter by 50%.
Rapidly freeze a part of the tissues in liquid nitrogen.
Transfer frozen tissues to −80°C freezer for storage.
Fix the rest part of the tissues in 4% paraformaldehyde for 48 hours.
Cut a section with a length of about 0.5 cm from the AAA segment with the largest external diameter.
Put the tissue section into a tissue embedding cassette.
Immerse the cassettes in tap water and rinse them with running water for 3–4 hours to remove paraformaldehyde.
Place the cassettes in an automatic benchtop tissue processor and select an appropriate program as follows: water for 10 minutes.
Mix 70% ethanol and immerse tissues for 2 hours.
Mix 80% ethanol and immerse tissues for 2 hours.
Mix 90% ethanol and immerse tissues for 2 hours.
Mix 95% ethanol (first batch) and immerse tissues for 1 hour.
Mix 95% ethanol (second batch) and immerse tissues for 1 hour.
Mix 100% ethanol (first batch) and immerse tissues for 1 hour.
Mix 100% ethanol (second batch) and immerse tissues for 1 hour.
Mix Histo-Clear I and immerse tissues for 45 minutes.
Mix Histo-Clear II and immerse tissues for 45 minutes.
Immerse tissues in paraffin I for 1.5 hours.
Immerse tissues in paraffin II for 1.5 hours.
Select appropriate-sized paraffin molds for tissues.
Dip tissue in paraffin-filled molds with cut-side down.
Place molds on cold plate to solidify paraffin.
Remove and store solidified paraffin blocks at 25°C.
Keep harvested tissues in 4% paraformaldehyde for 48 hours at 25°C.
Trim paraffin blocks using a rotary microtome until vascular lumen is exposed.
Immerse trimmed blocks in an ice-water mixture for 2 hours.
Cut paraffin tissues into consecutive 5 μm-thick slices.
Place tissue sections in 37°C warm water for spreading.
Gently pick up tissue sections with adhesion microscope slides.
Put 2-3 pieces of tissue on each slide.
Drain residual water off the slides.
Place slides on flattening table at 65°C for 2 hours.
Store slides in section box at 25°C.
Label tissue groups on the slides with a pencil.
Place sections in a multifunctional slide stainer and select the appropriate dewaxing program.
Heat sections at 65°C for 30 min.
Immerse sections in Histo-Clear I for 10 min.
Immerse sections in Histo-Clear II for 10 min.
Wash sections in 100% ethanol for 5 min.
Wash sections in 95% ethanol for 4 min.
Wash sections in 90% ethanol for 3 min.
Wash sections in 80% ethanol for 3 min.
Wash sections in 70% ethanol for 2 min.
Immerse sections in water I for 5 min.
Immerse sections in water II for 5 min.
Place dewaxed sections in hematoxylin staining solution for 3 min.
Wash sections in water to remove excess hematoxylin.
Differentiate sections in alcohol containing 1% hydrochloric acid until the cytoplasm is unstained and nucleus blue-purple.
Rinse sections in running water for 0.5–1 min until nuclei are blue.
Place sections in eosin staining solution for 3–5 min until cytoplasm is stained pink.
Wash sections in water to remove excess eosin.
Dehydrate sections in 80% ethanol for 5 s.
Dehydrate sections in 95% ethanol for 1 min.
Immerse sections in 100% ethanol I for 5 min.
Immerse sections in 100% ethanol II for 5 min.
Immerse sections in Histo-Clear I for 5 min.
Immerse sections in Histo-Clear II for 5 minutes.
Add a drop of neutral balsam on one side of each section and slowly cover with a coverslip to avoid air bubbles.
Place dewaxed sections in working Elastic Stain Solution from the kit for 15 minutes.
Wash sections in running tap water.
Dip sections in Differentiating solution for 15–20 times.
Rinse sections under running tap water.
Check elastic fiber staining under a microscope and repeat steps c to d if necessary until fibers are clearly stained black-blue.
Treat the sections with Sodium Thiosulfate Solution for 1 minute.
Wash sections in running tap water.
Stain sections in Van Gieson’s Solution from the kit for 2–5 minutes.
Dehydrate sections using 95% ethanol for 1 minute.
Immerse sections in 100% ethanol I for 5 minutes.
Immerse sections in 100% ethanol II for 5 minutes.
Treat sections with Histo-Clear I for 5 minutes.
Treat sections with Histo-Clear II for 5 minutes.
Add a drop of neutral balsam on one side of each section and slowly cover the coverslip to avoid air bubbles.
